 Home Opinion Taylor Fritz Taylor Fritz has made a very smart decision after missing out on the ATP Finals this year
 Matthew Johns Thu 12 November 2026 14:00, UK Add to Preferred Sources Taylor Fritz has already started making plans for 2027 after missing out on the ATP Finals so narrowly. 
 Fritz was beaten by Carlos Alcaraz at the Paris Masters last week, in a match where he was twice one point away from securing qualification to the ATP Finals .
 This ended any hopes of Fritz securing direct qualification to the ATP Finals, although he is still expected to be in Turin as the second alternate if two players withdraw.
 Fritz is also in action this week at the Stockholm Open , which could prove to be a genius decision from the American.
 Taylor Fritz has decided to get a head start in the race to the ATP Finals
 Fritz beat British player Cameron Norrie 7-5, 6-3 in his opening match in the Swedish capital to successfully book his place in the Stockholm Open quarter-finals.
 There may be some questioning Fritz’s decision to compete at an ATP 250 level tournament, particularly as the race to the ATP Finals this year is now over. However, with the race to the ATP Finals being over for this year, points players earn at the Stockholm Open this week will instead be counted towards the race to the 2027 ATP Finals.
 Therefore with Fritz remaining in Europe anyway to be alternate at the ATP Finals next week, he has made a very smart decision to compete in Stockholm.
 Fritz was just 149 points behind Rafael Jodar in qualifying for the ATP Finals this year, and by competing in Stockholm this week it enables him to have an advantage over the rest of his rivals who will likely be in the mix to play in Turin in 2027.
 This feels particularly relevant to someone like Fritz, who has had his 2026 season majorly disrupted due to tendonitis in his right knee, which forced him to take a break for most of the clay court season, and he is now making the right decision by taking advantage of a smaller tournament when he is feeling physically healthy.
 More Tennis News Fritz also knows that he can end the year ranked inside the top 10 for a fifth consecutive season with a deep run at the Stockholm Open.
 Which American ATP player will be the next to win a major title, where and when?
 Andy Roddick was the last American man to win a Grand Slam singles title – At the 2003 US Open…

 Fritz is the top seed at the Stockholm Open this week, and therefore should be the big favourite to take the title that has previously been won by the likes of Roger Federer , Bjorn Borg and John McEnroe .
 However, there is one name in the Stockholm field that stands out as the biggest threat to Fritz in the form of Lorenzo Musetti . Musetti, himself, has had a very disrupted 2026 season, but has recently found some form.
 This includes Musetti winning the title at the ATP 250 tournament in Lyon, where he actually beat Fritz in the final. Musetti’s victory in this final gave him a 5-3 lead in his head-to-head against Fritz, and he would likely feel confident if he played the American again in a potential semi-final in Stockholm.
 Before Fritz can even think about Musetti, he has a tricky quarter-final match against former world number four Holger Rune to overcome. Rune is also on a comeback of his own, having recently returned from a ruptured Achilles tendon that he actually suffered at the Stockholm Open last year.
 Fritz will be hoping to put a halt to Rune’s redemption in Stockholm, with the former winning two of their three previous meetings.
